payload.feature:
Fix the last Windows failure in decision 0046 slice (i), on branch fire/0046-boundary. Linux and macOS are green; Windows fails five cases in one suite, `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/boundary_verbs.rs`.

Read the archived change under `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i/`, decision 0046 with its addendum and erratum, and the proposed decision 0048. The requirement that governs this is the one naming the fixed environment an unboxed exec dispatch runs in, and its scenario "Windows starts its processes".

**The evidence, from the failing CI job.** Four `boundary_verbs` cases drive a real run that exits 2 (parked) where the test expects 0. One of them dumps its events, and the park reads:

    effect ... failed 1 of 1 attempt(s); last error: could not invoke the agent CLI: program not found; stderr tail:

So on Windows the unboxed exec dispatch cannot start its program at all. The same dispatch starts fine on Linux and macOS.

**The likely cause, which you must confirm rather than assume.** This slice starts an unboxed exec dispatch from an empty environment and sets exactly the keys the requirement lists — `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `PATH`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, and the bind-gated `CARGO_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME`, `NPM_CONFIG_CACHE`. That table is Unix-shaped. Windows resolves an executable using variables the table does not carry: `PATHEXT` decides that `bash` means `bash.exe`, and `SystemRoot`, `windir` and `COMSPEC` are required by the loader and by anything spawning a shell. With those absent from a cleared environment, "program not found" is exactly what a Windows spawn reports.

Confirm it, then fix the requirement and the code together: the fixed table keeps its Unix keys and gains, on Windows only, the process-startup variables Windows itself needs, inherited verbatim from the engine's environment and each only when set there — named explicitly in the requirement, not "whatever Windows wants", because a closed list is the point of the table. The security property the table exists for is unchanged: nothing of the operator's secrets travels, and the list stays closed and stated.

Update the delta requirement's text and its "Windows starts its processes" scenario in the archived change's spec **and** the promoted capability spec under `openspec/specs/`, so standing truth and the archive agree. If the archived change's text must move, say so in your notes; do not silently rewrite an archived artifact without recording it.

Add a unit test over the composed environment that asserts the exact key set per platform, so the Unix and Windows tables are both pinned and a later edit cannot drop one. It must run and mean something on Linux.

Constraints, binding: do not edit `contracts/*.v1..v8`, `realms.v1..v3`, `seat-record.v1..v3`, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/`, or `fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson`. Re-pin any witness or compose digest that moves. Any test driving a boxed step end to end skips under `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX`. Coverage is exact and literal.

Green before you finish: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and both `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify`. You cannot run Windows here; say what you could not verify and what evidence you relied on.

One more thing seen in the same job and probably unrelated: `anchor gap for init-in-place-...: git command failed: ["commit-tree", ...]: Author identity unknown`. Judge whether it is this slice's or the runner's; if it is the runner's, say so and leave it.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

result.notes: Committed b8b89a6. Confirmed mixed-case Path was dropped; the fourteen Windows startup keys already existed. Fixed Windows inherited-name matching, pinned both exact platform tables with Linux-executed regressions, and repaired the gate fixture's verbatim drive-path parser. Updated both requirements/scenarios and explicitly recorded the archive amendment in completion notes and proposed decision 0048. Formatting, clippy, workspace tests, both bundle compiles and literal coverage pass (21262 lines, 3306 branches, 2018 functions). Frozen files and digest pins are unchanged. Native Windows execution and attribution of the previously undumped inherited-environment failure remain unverified; evidence is CI run 34056215971, Rust's resolver and failing-then-passing Linux regressions. The unrelated runner Git identity gap is unchanged. Never pushed.

cargo test --workspace: 61 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed the complete delivery 1f3546a..b8b89a6 against the commission, archived framing and decisions 0046/0048. One unresolved finding: MEDIUM SECURITY — crates/brokkr-cli/tests/boundary_verbs.rs:352-356 adds a full event dump on failure to the plain-run test. That test removes hands, so Workspace::brokkr inherits the operator environment; GATE embeds the actual GH_TOKEN in result notes. A failed run after a result is recorded now prints that credential into test/CI diagnostics. Reproduced without real credentials: ran the exact plain-run test with GH_TOKEN=REVIEW_SYNTHETIC_GH_TOKEN_681f and BROKKR_HANDS_BOX set to the literal string [", "result":"fail] (brackets excluded), which makes the fixture return a valid fail record. The six-case current binary exits 101 and prints the synthetic token; the older five-case binary exits 101 without printing it. The forced failure is only a reproduction trigger; any failure after a credential-bearing result is recorded reaches the same dump. The implementer should supply a dummy GH_TOKEN to fixture children or redact credential-bearing diagnostics, and prove failure output excludes a planted parent token. No other correctness, simplicity or security findings. The production Windows lookup keeps the closed startup list and fixes mixed-case Path inheritance. Both platform table regressions and all six boundary_verbs cases pass normally, as do formatting and both bundle compiles. Inspected retained clippy/workspace/coverage evidence: 61 successful suite summaries, 1268 passing tests, and literal 21262/21262 lines, 3306/3306 branches, 2018/2018 functions. Frozen surfaces and witness/compose pins are unchanged. The archive amendment is explicitly recorded and its environment requirement/scenarios match standing truth. Native Windows execution remains unverified; relied on CI run 34056215971, Rust 1.98.0 resolver source and Linux regressions. The Git author-identity anchor gap is runner configuration outside this repair. No source edits, commits or task changes; only this required result file was written.

Closed the returned medium security finding in commit c2c637f. Both fixture launch paths now override GH_TOKEN with a fixed dummy. A subprocess regression reproduced the leak before the repair and now proves an actual failure event dump contains the dummy but excludes a planted parent token from stdout and stderr. All seven boundary tests, formatting, warning-free clippy, workspace tests, both bundle compiles and exact coverage pass (21262/21262 lines, 3306/3306 branches, 2018/2018 functions). Proposed decision 0048 records the repair. Production semantics, frozen surfaces and digest pins are unchanged; no further archive/spec edits. Native Windows remains unverified; prior CI/source evidence and limits remain documented. Runner Git identity is unchanged. Working tree clean; never pushed.
